Summary\r\n\r\nv2.12.0 is mostly a reliability release. It changes what kube-router's health check means so that failing syncs no longer get kube-router restarted, adds metrics to cover those failures instead, adds CNI configuration templates, and brings quite a few bug and security fixes to the Network Policy, Network Services, and Network Routes Controllers.\r\n\r\nUser-facing changes:\r\n\r\n* **`/healthz` now only reports liveness** - controllers now heartbeat at the start and end of every sync whether it succeeded or not, so a sync that keeps failing (a rule the kernel rejects, a route that can't be installed, a BGP peer that won't come up) no longer restarts kube-router into a `CrashLoopBackOff`. A failed initial sync in the Network Services Controller is also no longer fatal.\r\n  * If you were counting on restarts to surface sync failures, you'll want to alert on the new `kube_router_controller_sync_last_success` and `kube_router_controller_sync_failures_total` metrics instead. The [health](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/health.md) and [metrics](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/metrics.md) docs have the reasoning and some example alerts.\r\n* **CNI configuration templates** - the new `KUBE_ROUTER_CNI_CONF_TEMPLATE_FILE` env var has kube-router build its CNI config from a template and write the finished file itself, so the container runtime can't pick up a half-finished config on a freshly booted node (which showed up as transient \"no IP ranges specified\" errors). Also, a `.conflist` CNI config without a `bridge` plugin now fails at startup with a clear error instead of causing a panic later on. See the [user guide](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/user-guide.md#cni-configuration-templates) and the [example manifest](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/daemonset/generic-kuberouter-cni-conf-template.yaml).\r\n* **BFD improvements** - GoBGP v4.10.0 fixes a bug where a stale BFD administrative reset could kill the next BGP session and leave the peer flapping indefinitely ([#2189](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/issues/2189)), and the new `kube_router_bfd_peer_info` metric exposes the session state of each BFD peer.\r\n* **Network policy fixes**:\r\n  * Egress rules with a named port and no `to` peers used to allow any destination on the resolved port number, and are now limited to pods that actually expose that port. Pods could also end up in the wrong named port entries.\r\n  * Some chain and set names could collide. Because the fix changes chain and set names, expect kube-router to recreate them on the first sync after upgrading (the old ones are cleaned up automatically).\r\n  * Full syncs on the iptables backend are a lot cheaper on nodes with many pods, since kube-router no longer copies and scans the whole filter table once per pod (in our benchmark with 80 pods, a sync went from about 150 ms and 90 MB to about 0.5 ms and 0.2 MB).\r\n* **Service proxy fixes**:\r\n  * Services whose namespace, name, and port name joined into the same key (port `http-alt` on `web` and port `alt` on `web-http`, for example) collided, which left one without a VIP and had the other load balancing to both services' pods.\r\n  * DSR setup now only enters the network namespace of pods in the service's own namespace, where before a selectorless service could point it at pods in other namespaces or at the host itself.\r\n* **Consistent backends for hashing schedulers** - endpoints are now sorted for the `sh`, `dh`, and `mh` schedulers so that the same client reaches the same backend no matter which node it lands on. Existing IPVS services keep their current order, so check out the [troubleshooting doc](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/troubleshoot.md#inconsistent-backend-selection-with-hashing-schedulers) if you need to reset them.\r\n* **BGP peer passwords no longer leak into logs** - when the `kube-router.io/peers` annotation failed to parse, the logged error could include the surrounding YAML, base64 encoded passwords and all.\r\n* **Example manifests refreshed** - the daemonsets in `daemonset/` now gate liveness behind a startup probe, use `dnsPolicy: Default` and `cniVersion` 1.0.0, and drop RBAC grants kube-router no longer needs. The proxy-only and firewall-only manifests now use a service account instead of a host kubeconfig and leave the CNI config alone. If you've based your deployment on any of these, be sure to diff them before upgrading.\r\n\r\nNotable maintenance changes:\r\n\r\n* Go - 1.26.10 -> 1.27.3\r\n* Kubernetes client libraries - v0.36.3 -> v0.37.2\r\n* GoBGP - v4.8.0 -> v4.10.0\r\n\r\n## Contributions\r\n\r\nThanks to @twz123, @mrueg, @rkojedzinszky, @damex, @spicysharkco, and @cwaynej for their contributions to this release.\r\n\r\nA special welcome to @spicysharkco and @cwaynej on their first contributions!\r\n\r\nThanks as well to @catherinetcai for moving our CI over to Blacksmith. Summary\r\n\r\nv2.11.0 adds an experimental nftables backend for network policies and BFD support for external BGP peers. It also contains bug and security fixes for the Network Routes Controller (BGP password logging leak) and Network Services Controller (dual-stack NodePort programming), and behavior changes around CNI config loading and MTU autodetection.\r\n\r\nUser-facing changes:\r\n\r\n- **Experimental nftables backend for network policies** - new `--use-nftables-for-netpol` flag to have the Network Policy Controller use nftables instead of iptables. Please review the docs (https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/nftables.md) for instructions on how to enable this feature. \r\n-  **BFD for BGP external peers** - BFD is now available for external BGP peers. Please review the docs (https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/bgp.md) for the new CLI flags and configurations required to enable BFD.\r\n- **kube-router no longer exits on startup if node MTU can't be autodetected** - previously, kube-router would terminate if node MTU cannot be autodetected. Now, it logs an error and leaves the CNI configuration for the bridge interface without an explicit MTU.\r\n- **kube-router now rejects stray positional CLI arguments** - kube-router will exit and log errors for unrecognized flags instead of silently handling them\r\n- **Dual-stack services now program IPv6 NodePorts** - services now appropriately get their IPv6 NodePort programmed\r\n\r\nNotable maintenance changes:\r\n\r\n* Go - 1.26.3 -> 1.26.6\r\n* Kubernetes client libraries - v0.36.1 -> v0.36.3\r\n* GoBGP - v4.5.0 -> v4.8.0\r\n\r\n## Contributions\r\nThanks to @thomasferrandiz and Summary\r\n\r\nv2.10.0 is a feature-and-hardening release focused on tighter network policy defaults, broader IPv6 parity in the\r\nNetwork Routes Controller, and a refresh of the Kubernetes/Go toolchain. New user-facing functionality:\r\n\r\n- **Default-deny pod-to-pod traffic in NPC** - new --netpol-default-deny mode that lets the Network Policy\r\nController enforce a default-deny posture for pod<->pod traffic when no policy matches. See the new\r\ndocs section (https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/user-guide.md) on how it works.\r\n- **IPv6 support for customImportReject in NRC** - the custom import-reject prefix list now works for IPv6, and\r\nthe default V6 default-route is properly rejected from peers (companion fix to the V4 behavior).\r\n- **Configurable healthcheck bind address** - new flag to control which address the healthcheck server listens on,\r\nuseful for multi-homed nodes and stricter network segmentation.\r\n- **EndpointSlice service.kubernetes.io/headless label recognized** - NSC now treats headless services correctly\r\nwhen sourced from EndpointSlices.\r\n- **LoadBalancer + NPC hardening** - additional safety in the load balancer and network policy controllers,\r\nincluding control-character stripping in comments and an explicit error when deny by default is configured\r\nwithout a range.\r\n\r\nOn the maintenance side, this release bumps Go to 1.26.3 and the Kubernetes client libraries to v0.36 (which drove\r\nthe Go bump), updates GoBGP to v4.5.0, refreshes vishvananda/netlink, replaces docker/docker with\r\nmoby/moby/client, and pulls in the usual round of dependabot bumps across golang.org/x/*, gRPC, AWS SDK v2,\r\nCodeQL, and other CI actions. There are no intentional breaking changes for end users in this release -- existing\r\nflags and behaviors are preserved, with default-deny gated behind its opt-in flag.\r\n\r\n## Breaking Changes\r\n\r\n### GoBGP Admin Server Binds to Localhost by Default\r\n\r\nThis release introduces a new command-line flag to configure the address of GoBGP admin server:\r\n* `--gobgp-admin-address` (default: `127.0.0.1`) -- Address for GoBGP server. Used in combination with gobgp-admin-port to expose GoBGP for administrative purposes. Setting this to empty string will default the address to 127.0.0.1. \r\n\r\nIn previous kube-router versions, the GoBGP admin server, when enabled, would bind to the node's primary IP address by default. We've changed this to default to 127.0.0.1 to address https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/security/advisories/GHSA-v5mh-h5hx-7v92, which was reported by @offset (thank you!)\r\n\r\nPlease review the [user guide](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/user-guide.md) and [BGP docs](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/bgp.md) for more details. \r\n\r\nIf you have questions or concerns, please reach out via the #kube-router channel on\r\n[Kubernetes Slack](https://kubernetes.slack.com/messages/C8DCQGTSB/) or email admin@kube-router.io.\r\n\r\n## Summary\r\nv2.9.0 is a small security release that changes the binding address for the GoBGP admin server to the more secure default of localhost. \r\n\r\n## Security Notice\r\n\r\n**This release contains an important security fix. A GitHub Security Advisory (GHSA) & CVE with full details will be\r\npublished soon.** We are releasing the fix ahead of the advisory to give operators time to upgrade.\r\n\r\n**Edit on 3/17/2026** - This release addresses the vulnerabilities found and reported by @b0b0haha and @j311yl0v3u (thank you!) via [GHSA-phqm-jgc3-qf8g](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/security/advisories/GHSA-phqm-jgc3-qf8g) and CVE-2026-32254\r\n\r\n**We strongly recommend that all users upgrade to v2.8.0 as soon as possible.** This is especially critical for\r\nmulti-tenant clusters or clusters where untrusted users have the ability to create or modify Service resources.\r\n\r\nIf you have questions or concerns, please reach out via the `#kube-router` channel on\r\n[Kubernetes Slack](https://kubernetes.slack.com/messages/C8DCQGTSB/) or email `admin@kube-router.io`.\r\n\r\n## Breaking Changes\r\n\r\n### Service IP Range Validation on by Default\r\n\r\nThis release introduces a new command-line flag which is by default enabled:\r\n\r\n- `--strict-external-ip-validation` (default: `true`) -- When enabled, externalIPs and loadBalancerIPs on Service\r\n  resources are validated against the configured `--service-external-ip-range` and `--loadbalancer-ip-range` flags.\r\n  IPs that fall outside the allowed ranges or that conflict with the cluster IP range are rejected. When no ranges are\r\n  configured and strict mode is enabled, all externalIPs and loadBalancerIPs are rejected (default-deny). We recommend\r\n  enabling this flag on all clusters.\r\n\r\nSee the [user guide](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/user-guide.md) for configuration details.\r\n\r\n**For this release the kube-router team STRONGLY recommends that you either:**\r\n\r\n* Have all of your service ranges defined correctly via the `--service-external-ip-range` and `--loadbalancer-ip-range` flags\r\n  and ensure that all of your current services have VIPs that are contained in the ranges defined **before upgrading to v2.8.0**\r\n* Set `--strict-external-ip-validation=false` as one of your options to kube-router **before upgrading to v2.8.0.** Note\r\n  doing this in a multi-tenant cluster is not recommended by the project.\r\n\r\n### Prometheus Metric Changes\r\n\r\n`kube_router_controller_bgp_peers` has been replaced with the new metric `kube_router_bgp_peer_info` which contains\r\nmore information about the peer's state as well as includes externally configured peers (whereas the previous metric\r\nonly showed kube-router based peering info).\r\n\r\n## Summary\r\n\r\nv2.8.0 brings a security hardening release focused on service IP validation, along with SCTP support, a new BGP peer\r\ninfo metric, and extensive documentation improvements.\r\n\r\nAdditionally, with this release the kube-router project officially welcomes @catherinetcai to our small maintainer\r\ngroup! Big thanks for all of the support she's already provided and we look forward to seeing how she improves\r\nkube-router in the months / years to come. :)\r\n\r\n### SCTP Support\r\n\r\nkube-router now supports the SCTP protocol in Service resources, extending the existing TCP and UDP support. This includes\r\nproper handling in IPVS service proxy, iptables rules, and node port specifications.\r\n\r\n### BGP Peer Info Metric\r\n\r\nA new Prometheus metric `kube_router_bgp_peer_info` has been added, providing detailed information about BGP peer\r\nstate. The previous `controller_bgp_peers` metric name has been replaced.\r\n\r\n### Documentation Overhaul\r\n\r\nThis release includes a significant documentation refresh:\r\n\r\n- Updated and modernized the user guide, architecture docs, and troubleshooting guide\r\n- Added table of contents to long-form documentation\r\n- Corrected spelling and grammar throughout\r\n- Added a code of conduct and pull request template\r\n- Added AI agent guidelines for contributors\r\n- Added a supported versions statement\r\n- Updated the architecture diagram to include the Load Balancer Allocator controller\r\n\r\n## Contributions\r\n\r\nThanks to the community members who contributed to this release:\r\n\r\n- SCTP support: @damex\r\n- BGP peer info metric: @damex\r\n\r\n## Changelog\r\n\r\n* Summary\r\n\r\nWelcome to another full minor release update of kube-router! This one comes with several large-ish fixes along with a\r\nfew improvements to functionality.\r\n\r\nFirst off the major dependency version changes:\r\n\r\n* Bump Go 1.25.1 -> 1.25.7\r\n* CNI plugins v1.8.0 -> v1.9.0\r\n* GoBGP 3.37.0 -> 4.2.0\r\n* Add bugfixes to iptables wrapper script from upstream\r\n\r\n### Node Annotation Consolidation\r\n\r\nv2.7.0 also comes with a major change to the way BGP peers can be configured via node annotations. Node annotations can\r\nstill be configured with the previous method of comma separated values. However, they can also now be configured using a\r\nconsolidated embedded yaml form:\r\n\r\n```yaml\r\nkubectl annotate node <kube-node> \\\r\nkube-router.io/peers=\"$(cat <<'EOF'\r\n- remoteip: 192.168.1.99\r\n  remoteasn: 65000\r\n  password: U2VjdXJlUGFzc3dvcmQK\r\n- remoteip: 192.168.1.100\r\n  remoteasn: 65000\r\n  password: U2VjdXJlUGFzc3dvcmQK\r\nEOF\r\n)\"\r\n```\r\n\r\nSee [using consolidated annotations](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/bgp.md#using-consolidated-annotation) for more information.\r\n\r\n### Other Notable Changes\r\n\r\n* Add better unit testing to Network Services Controller (`--run-service-proxy`) to prevent future regressions - This\r\n  hopefully helps curb one of the largest sources of functionality regressions over the past several years within\r\n  kube-router\r\n* Configure AFI SAFI for dual stack clusters regardless of graceful restart setting - Previously, this was configured for the\r\n  primary IP family (becuase GoBGP does this by default), but the secondary family would only get AFI SAFI\r\n  configurations if graceful restart was configured (`--bgp-graceful-restart`)\r\n* Correctly configure TCPMSS for IPv6 tunnels - Previously TCPMSS clamping was a one-size-fits-all based on the size of\r\n  IPv4 headers. Now they are properly configured per family\r\n* Retry certain netlink calls which fixes early start race conditions - Some users noticed a race condition on ip link\r\n  setup when kube-router was starting as the node's OS was also starting. This should fix that edge case.\r\n\r\n## Contributions\r\n\r\nThanks to all of the community members that helped contribute to this release! Your volunteered time is what makes open\r\nsource projects like this one still viable!\r\n\r\nContributors to this release:\r\n\r\n* Documentation fixes: @xieyubo\r\n* Go Safecast bug fixes and unit test efficiencies: @ccoVeille\r\n* Consolidated node annotations & fixing netlink retries: @catherinetcai\r\n* Fix TCPMSS clamping for IPv6: @rkojedzinszky\r\n* Keeping all of our dependencies up to date and helping with our builds: @mrueg\r\n\r\n## Changelog\r\n\r\n* da980503 - Summary\r\n\r\nIt has been more than half a year since our last official kube-router release, so I think we're more than past time to do so. Additionally, there have been quite a few items that have been fixed or upgraded.\r\n\r\n### Highlights & Changed Functionality\r\n\r\n* The Network Services Controller (enabled via `--run-service-proxy`) now fetches metrics when the metrics URL is hit rather than on the sync period (`--ipvs-sync-period`). This allows for more fine-grained and up-to-date metrics on IPVS services. (Thanks @rkojedzinszky!)\r\n* Service's `externalIP` and `LoadBalancerIP` are now labels on IPVS metrics which can increase cardinality, but also provides better visibility for services. Prior to this, only the `ClusterIP` or `NodePort` labels were added to metrics.\r\n* The GoBGP port can be changed or disabled via `--gpbgp-admin-port` to create more secure / flexible deployments of kube-router\r\n* We converted a lot of exec's  out to `iproute2` into `netlink` library calls, making the code more idiomatic, faster, and less fragile to userspace tooling changes\r\n* When both DSR and Maglev is enabled on a service kube-router will automatically enable the kernel option `sloppy_tcp` for IPVS which allows for greater service routing consistency when transitioning nodes (Thanks @AnupamGhosh!)\r\n* All references to Endpoints has been removed since the API is now fully deprecated and EndpointSlices is now used behind the scenes\r\n\r\n### Fixed Issues\r\n\r\n* [1895](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/issues/1895) - IPv6 NDP NA/NS dropped when using egress network policy\r\n* [1875](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/issues/1875) - Collect service statistics real-time\r\n* [1888](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/issues/1860) - Resilience to TCP SYN Node Loss\r\n* [1816](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/issues/1816) - support change the default port of GoBGP\r\n* [1614](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/issues/1614) - Fix CLI Options - --master doesn't work without --kubeconfig\r\n\r\n### Library Updates\r\n\r\n* Go Version: `1.23.6` -> `1.25.1`\r\n* Alpine Version: `3.21` -> `3.22`\r\n* Go Releaser Version: `v2.5.0` -> `v2.12.2`\r\n* GoBGP Version: `v3.29.0` -> `v3.37.0`\r\n* CNI Plugin Version: `v1.6.2` -> `v1.8.0`\r\n* Kubernetes Libraries: `v1.31.3` -> `v1.34.1`\r\n\r\n## Contributions\r\n\r\nSpecial thanks to @rkojedzinszky, @AnupamGhosh, @qbnit0 for contributing to kube-router and helping make this release possible!\r\n\r\n## Changelog\r\n\r\n* 8bf2e563 - feat(cni): update v1.6.2 -> v1.8.0 `<Aaron Summary\r\n\r\nThis update is mainly a dependency and docker image base update. For a long time, kube-router has been stalled on Alpine 3.18 because of a breaking change with the upstream iptables user space. However, this was fixed in `iptables-1.8.11` which was released in November and then was integrated into Alpine 3.21 early this Month. See https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/issues/1789 for more information.\r\n\r\nThis should make kube-router much more tolerant of iptables / nftables rules added by recent versions of the netfilter userspaces.\r\n\r\nThis release does contain a few prominent fixes since the last release of v2.4.1:\r\n\r\n* `ipset.Save()` was introduced at the start of the NetworkPolicyController resolving a race condition between the NetworkPolicyController (`--run-firewall`) and the NetworkServiceController (`--run-service-proxy`). See #1806 (thanks @alexcriss for reporting this and being patient while we tried to reproduce)\r\n* Internal cluster traffic is now properly excluded from NAT conditions which resolves a regression that was introduced in the v2.3 release line. See: #1778 (thanks @zerkms for reporting this)\r\n\r\nOther major dependency updates:\r\n\r\n* Bundled CNI plugins have been updated from v1.4.0 -> v1.6.2\r\n* Go version has been updated from v1.22.3 -> v1.23.6\r\n\r\n## Contributions\r\n\r\nSpecial thanks to @rbrtbnfgl and @dsseng for their contributions to this release!\r\n\r\n## Changelog\r\n\r\n* 85e429e9 - doc(RELEASE.md): update release docs Summary\r\n\r\nThis release fixes a lot of issues that have been present since the release of v2.0.0. v2.0.0 has been gaining adoption slowly and it has only been recently that users have been reporting some of the issues related with dual-stack configurations.\r\n\r\nThe big additions for this release include:\r\n\r\n* Fixing broken compatibility with iptables-legacy systems experienced with the upstream kube-router container since version v2.1.0 (which is when Alpine 3.19 was introduced). There are now tests to ensure that this type of regression doesn't happen again.\r\n* Fixes IPv6 network policy which has been substantially broken since v2.0.0. When IPv6 network policy was introduced, it was missed that iptables statements need to reference these sets via the `inet6` prefix in order to use them correctly. As such, most network policies were not correctly applying.\r\n* kube-router no longer activates the hairpin controller which was introduced in v2.1.0, instead relying on user's correctly configuring their CNI with `hairpinMode: true` (see https://www.kube-router.io/docs/user-guide/#hairpin-mode for more details)\r\n* Adds fallback logic for referencing `rt_tables`, the path of which changed in versions of iproute2 v6.5.0 and above. Users that have newer systems, enable DSR, and run kube-router within a container should check to ensure this file is mounted correctly within the kube-router container.\r\n* kube-router no longer tries and fails to enter pods to setup DSR for pods that are not scheduled on it's node\r\n* kube-router no longer tries and fails to setup DSR for pods that are part of the host's network\r\n* Fixes `--cleanup-config` mode which has been broken since v2.0.0 (please see docs for updated examples of how to run this from within a container)\r\n\r\n### Special Note for Users that Run Hairpin Mode Enabled Services\r\n\r\nIf you use hairpin mode either as a service annotation or a CLI parameter to kube-router, we recommend that you check your CNI configuration file to ensure that you are setting `\"hairpinMode\":true` on the `bridge` CNI plugin. This is the only way that hairpin mode will work correctly as the previous hairpin controller built into kube-router has now been disabled as it was a tricky implementation and had significant problems with irregular containers.\r\n\r\nIf you find that you need to add this to your CNI config file, please ensure that kubelet has been restarted, and that any pods that rely on hairpinning have been restarted as well.\r\n\r\nSee https://www.kube-router.io/docs/user-guide/#hairpin-mode for more information.\r\n\r\n## Contributions\r\n\r\nA big thanks @elchenberg & @xujunjie-cover for Summary\r\n\r\nThe major theme of this kube-router release is to make kube-router fully conformant with the end-to-end upstream sig-network tests. These are tests that the Kubernetes project provides for testing significant networking features and becoming conformant with the tests means that the networking functionality of kube-router is more consistent with other network providers like kube-proxy, Calico, and Cilium.\r\n\r\n### Major New Features / Fixes\r\n\r\n* kube-router's init container now installs CNI plugins when they are missing. The location for these plugins can be controlled by setting the environment variable `HOST_BIN_PATH` within the init container, but will default to `/opt/cni/bin`. This is something that all major Kubernetes networking providers do, but kube-router has not done in the past. For more information on CNI plugins, please see: https://github.com/containernetworking/plugins\r\n* kube-router now implements `.spec.healthCheckNodePort` which has long been a part of the [Kubernetes service specification](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.29/#servicespec-v1-core), but kube-router hasn't implemented it until now. This port is meant to give visibility about whether or not an endpoint for a service exists on a node to workloads outside the Kubernetes cluster. If a service endpoint is on the node, then this port returns a 200 HTTP response, otherwise it returns a 503 HTTP response if no endpoint exists on the node. By choosing a node that contains an endpoint, a client can ensure [source IP preservation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/access-application-cluster/create-external-load-balancer/#preserving-the-client-source-ip).\r\n* Hairpinning in kube-router is now fixed. kube-router now has a dedicated controller to ensuring that the `veth` interface inside the container is in promiscuous mode. This used to be handled by `kubelet` and then it was handled by `docker-shim` and then it was removed entirely. As far as I can tell, it was never ported to `containerd` or `cri-o`. Without this functionality, return traffic ends up getting black-holed before it is routed outside of the container. For more details see: https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/commit/0f3714b9b758f24de0b1911c148bdba8d87de9b6\r\n* Users can now specify `--metrics-addr` to choose the IP address that kube-router listens on when providing Prometheus metrics\r\n* Users can now specify custom protocol timeouts for IPVS services exposed by kube-router\r\n  * `--service-tcp-timeout` - (default: `0s` preserves system value, typically 900 seconds)\r\n  * `--service-tcpfin-timeout` - (default: `0s` preserves system value, typically 120 seconds)\r\n  * `--service-udp-timeout` - (default: `0s` preserves system value, typically 300 seconds)\r\n* kube-router now abides by the service label `service.kubernetes.io/service-proxy-name`. Setting this label to something other than `kube-router` will result in kube-router ignoring the service\r\n* kube-router now honors `spec.internalTrafficPolicy` and implements `spec.externalTrafficPolicy` correctly. For more information see: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/networking/virtual-ips/#traffic-policies for more information\r\n\r\n### Backward Compatibility Breaks\r\n\r\nkube-router now serves traffic to endpoints that that have a status of either `ready` or `serving`. See: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/endpoint-slices/#conditions for more information on the differences between these conditions. Before this release, kube-router only served traffic to `ready` endpoints, which improperly ignored pods that were in `Terminating` status. This change makes kube-router compliant with the upstream standards.\r\n\r\nThe release switches from Alpine base `3.18` to `3.19` which changes the iptables backend from [iptables to nftables](https://wiki.alpinelinux.org/wiki/Release_Notes_for_Alpine_3.19.0#iptables-nft). This is a pretty big change, since the two backends are not mixable. **_The kube-router project recommends coupling this upgrade with a rolling restart of the nodes in your cluster so that the iptables rules get flushed alongside the upgrade._**\r\n\r\n### Other Notes\r\n\r\n* If you're running kube-router in a container and use hairpinning, make sure that `hostPID: true` is set on your kube-router pod. This is the only way that kube-router is able to properly set the `veth` interface into promiscuous mode. This attribute has now been added to all of the [official kube-router DeaemonSet YAML files](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/tree/master/daemonset)\r\n\r\n### Major Dependency Updates\r\n\r\nThis release also updates:\r\n\r\n* Alpine base container from `3.18` to `3.19`\r\n* Go from `v1.20` to `v1.21`\r\n* Kubernetes from `v1.28` to `v1.29`\r\n\r\n## Summary\r\n\r\nkube-router v2.0.0 is a major release that the project has been working on for almost a year. We're very excited to finally enable some long-requested features.\r\n\r\nIts worth noting, that almost 50% of the existing code base had to be modified in order to bring this release to fruition. We've done testing via the several release candidates that we've released over the last few months (huge thanks to all of the users that engaged that by submitting fixes or reporting bugs), but I'm sure that there are still a few out there that we haven't caught yet.\r\n\r\n**The project recommends that users approach deploying this release to their production critical clusters with caution.** If you do find a bug, please open a new GitHub Issue with the `Report a v2.0.0 Release Issue` issue type so that we can resolve it as soon as possible.\r\n\r\n### Major New Features\r\n\r\n* Dual-Stack implemented in all kube-router controllers (e.g. `--run-firewall`, `--run-router`, `--run-loadbalancer`, & `--run-service-proxy`)\r\n* IPAM management for `LoadBalancer` service types (previously kube-router would only perform BGP, firewall, and proxy functionality and users would need to supplement kube-router with something like MetalLB to get IPs from a pool for their `LoadBalancer` services)\r\n* FoU tunneling capability added for pod networking (previously only `ipip` was supported)\r\n\r\n### Backward Compatibility Breaks\r\n\r\nYou'll also notice that this has been tagged as a major release version. This is due to the fact that there are breaking changes in this version of kube-router that are not backwards compatible with previous versions of kube-router.\r\n\r\nTunnel names have changed, so if you run kube-router with an overlay network (ipip tunnels), you'll want to deploy this update carefully. At this point, the project recommends doing a rolling-reboot of nodes after the application (or as part of) of this release to ensure that unused tunnels are properly cleaned up and don't have a negative impact on traffic flows.\r\n\r\nAs part of this work, kube-router now needs to be able to `get`, `list`, and `watch` `EndpointSlice` objects. **Please make sure to update your ClusterRole RBAC before deploying this release if you use kube-router with the `--run-service-proxy` functionality enabled or you'll get an error.** For examples of this RBAC please see the [daemonset examples](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/tree/master/daemonset).\r\n\r\n### Other Notes\r\n\r\nDual-stack handling is fairly complex and it comes with a few gotchas. Users that want to enable dual-stack features should carefully read the [IPv6 / Dual-Stack Support in kube-router](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/ipv6.md) documentation to ensure that they fully understand the feature set, requirements, and limitations.\r\n\r\nIf you want to run the new load balancer controller (e.g. `--run-loadbalancer`) kube-router will need some additional RBAC and requires a few environment variables set. See [load-balancer allocation docs](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/load-balancer-allocator.md) for more information.\r\n\r\nFor more information on enabling or migrating to FoU tunneling and any caveats on doing so, please see the [Tunnels in kube-router](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/tunnels.md) documentation.\r\n\r\nNow that kube-router has dual-stack capability, it doesn't make sense to have an annotation that can only represent a single pod CIDR any longer. As such, with this release we are announcing the deprecation of the `kube-router.io/pod-cidr` annotation in favor of the new `kube-router.io/pod-cidrs` annotation see the [IPv6 / Dual-Stack Support in kube-router](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/ipv6.md) documentation for more information.\r\n\r\n### Major Dependency Updates\r\n\r\nThis release also updates:\r\n\r\n* Alpine base container from `3.17` to `3.18`\r\n* Go from `v1.19` to `v1.20`\r\n* Kubernetes from `v1.25` to `v1.27`\r\n* GoBGP from `v3.11.0` to `v3.17.0`.\r\n\r\n## Contributions\r\n\r\nA release this big would not be possible without an awesome community. Thanks so much to all of the following people that helped play a part in this release: @brandond, @iggy, @whooo, @BoleynSu, @k-raval, @rwagoner, @vadorovsky, @thomasferrandiz, and @mrueg \r\n\r\n## Changelog (from v1.6.0 - Summary\r\n\r\nThe big headline of this release is support for dual-stack capabilities in the Network Services Controller (`--proxy` option). This was the last major outstanding feature milestone that was left to round out the v2.0.0 release. Now the entire kube-router code base has support for dual-stack capabilities.\r\n\r\nAs part of this work, kube-router now needs to be able to `get`, `list`, and `watch` `EndpointSlice` objects. **Please make sure to update your ClusterRole RBAC before deploying this release if you use kube-router with the `--proxy` functionality enabled or you'll get an error.** For examples of this RBAC please see the [daemonset examples from the prep-v2.0 branch](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/tree/prep-v2.0/daemonset).\r\n\r\nI want to make this release candidate available for the community to test for the next 1 - 2 weeks, and get a chance to resolve any open issues. After this, if the release candidate is stable, I'll merge the `prep-v2.0` branch to `master` and make an official `v2.0.0` release. This release has been a long time in coming and I'm excited to get it out there! A huge thanks to everyone that has helped test it and contributed to it!\r\n\r\nAdditionally, this release fixed a significant performance regression with Network Policies that was introduced in the v2.0.0 codebase during dual-stack implementation.\r\n\r\nThis release also updates Go from `1.19` to `1.20` and adds support for Kubernetes `v1.27`. We also upgraded our Alpine base version from `3.17` to `3.18` and GoBGP from `v3.11.0` to `v3.17.0`.\r\n\r\n## Contributions\r\n\r\nBig thanks goes to @brandond (and the k3s project) for finding and fixing the Network Policy performance issues and also adding additional metrics to the Network Policy Controller for increased observability.\r\n\r\nThanks @iggy for adding RISC-V 64 support for kube-router binaries. We are not yet building official container images for RISC-V 64 because Alpine doesn't yet officially support it, but when they do we'll enable container builds for RISC-V64 as well.\r\n\r\n## Summary\r\n\r\nThis is a pre-release or release candidate for the upcoming v2.0.0 release of kube-router. The most prominent feature of this release is the addition of dual-stack support for some parts of kube-router. With this release candidate, the following functions have been upgraded to be dual-stack compatible:\r\n\r\n* CNI Supports Dual-Stack\r\n* Router / BGP Supports Dual-Stack\r\n* Network Policies Supports Dual-Stack\r\n\r\nThe major outlier here being the `Proxy (--run-service-proxy)` portion of kube-router has not had dual-stack support integrated yet. Also, this represents a major refactor on the kube-router code base, so it would be good to get this tested in at least a few different environments before forming a full release.\r\n\r\nYou'll also notice that this has been tagged as a major release version. This is due to the fact that there are breaking changes in this version of kube-router that are not backwards compatible with previous versions of kube-router. Specifically, tunnel names have changed, so if you run kube-router with an overlay network (ipip tunnels), you'll want to deploy this update carefully. At this point, the project recommends doing a rolling-reboot of nodes after the application of this release candidate to ensure that unused tunnels are properly cleaned up and don't have a negative impact on traffic flows.\r\n\r\nMore details about this release will be shared in the IPv6 / Dual-Stack documentation page shortly: https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/docs/ipv6.md\r\n\r\n## Contributions\r\n\r\nThe kube-router project would like to give a big thanks to @vadorovsky and @thomasferrandiz who graciously contributed all of the dual-stack functionality for the Network Policy Controller!\r\n\r\n## Changelog\r\n\r\n* a9b8adf1 - fix(NPC): add warning for unsupported family `<Aaron U'Ren>`\r\n* 74a08036 - fix(NPC): don't add chains for missing family `<Aaron U'Ren>`\r\n* abcefb4e - doc(bgp.md): clean up grammar and syntax `<Aaron U'Ren>`\r\n* f4668fdf - fix(NPC/pod): check drop policy on ipv4 & ipv6 `<Aaron U'Ren>`\r\n* 6bd6d94d - fix(bgp_policies): add empty DS set checking `<Aaron U'Ren>`\r\n* ae15ebbd - fact(bgp_policies): rename clusterIPPrefixSet -> serviceVIPIPPrefixSet `<Aaron U'Ren>`\r\n* ed29baa9 - fact(bgp_policies): abstract get DS for GoBGP `<Aaron U'Ren>`\r\n* 6a1bab23 - fix(ecmp_vip): handle ipv4 & ipv6 protocols `<Aaron U'Ren>`\r\n* 437da143 - test(bgp_policies_test): add local address `<Aaron U'Ren>`\r\n* 3129bf26 - fix(node): do nil checking on FindBestIP util funcs `<Aaron U'Ren>`\r\n* 8183b182 - fix(NRC): ensure local addr IP is bindable early `<Aaron U'Ren>`\r\n* bd0d00ff - fix(bgp_peers): adv. Change Log Highlights\r\n\r\nThis adds a bunch of fixes for some small to medium sized issues with the 1.3.0 release. Notable changes include:\r\n* `--cleanup-config` flag should now be more comprehensive. There were a couple of bugs introduced in the 1.3 release that caused this flag to not function at all. These have been fixed. Additionally, it now cleans up most, if not all kube-router artifacts, where before it would leave some lingering parts of the Network Policy Controller.\r\n* `injectRoutes()`, the part of the Network Routes Controller that is responsible for injecting host routes based on BGP advertisements, has been completely overhauled.\r\n  * Routes are now cleaned up and removed from the host when nodes leave. This prevents bugs around black-hole routes that are created when nodes are decommissioned and that IP space is later reused by a new node.\r\n  * Performance is improved by checking if the route is a withdrawal first, rather than adding the route and then immediately removing it\r\n  * Logging has been updated to no longer be so spammy for default actions\r\n  * Code has been refactored to be easier to read and understand\r\n* IPVS metrics are now removed after the service is deleted rather than being continuously posted to prometheus (thanks @bhcleek!)\r\n* kube-router nodes are now protected from default route BGP advertisements. Before this, kube-router had the potential to overwrite the default route on the node causing the node to no longer be contactable (thanks @lucasmundim!)\r\n* Additional ipset locking was missing causing some errors around multiple invocations. This has been fixed.\r\n\r\n## Full Changelog\r\n\r\n* d173c988 - (HEAD -> master, tag: v1.3.1, origin/master, origin/HEAD) Update to go-1.16.7 and go dependencies (3 days ago) <Manuel Rüger>\r\n* are happy to announce the second release candidate for kube-router 0.1.0\r\n\r\nIn this release we have focused on introducing instrumentation to monitor metrics and health in kube-router for ease of operations, some minor bug fixes, adjustments to the logging output as well as introduced the BGP graceful restart function to enable zero downtime upgrades in supported environments.\r\n\r\n## Action required\r\nIf you previously used the metrics on port 8080 and wish to keep using this port you must set it at kube-router start using `--metrics-port` as the default now is 0, disabled\r\n\r\n## Logging\r\nA lot of the output from kube-router has had logging levels added to prevent spamming the logs with normal operations and debug output. To run kube-router in verbose mode for debugging please add `--v=3` to the start options.\r\n\r\n## Metrics\r\nWe have added a sample [Grafana](https://grafana.com/) dashboard & the possibility to change what port and path the metrics are exposed at. You can read more about the functionality [here](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/Documentation/metrics.md)\r\n\r\n## Health checks\r\nkube-router now comes with togglable health endpoint to monitor the status of your kube-router deployment. Read more about the functionality and how to enable it [here](https://github.com/cloudnativelabs/kube-router/blob/master/Documentation/health.md)\r\n\r\n## Local services\r\nSupport for service.spec externalTrafficPolicy=Local has been added. It takes precedence over kube-router.io/service.local annotation. Read more about externalTrafficPolicy [here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/access-application-cluster/create-external-load-balancer/) \r\n\r\n## BGP graceful restart\r\nSupport has been added in this version for [graceful BGP restarts](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4724). To enable it start kube-router with `--bgp-graceful-restart`. When peering with global peers make sure they support this mode before enabling\r\n\r\n## Notable Bug Fixes\r\n- A regression was introduced in RC1 where GoBGP would panic when adding nodes in some cases.
